examples.ko: 남의 비밀을 캐는 건 정말 악취미예요.
examples.en: Digging into other people's secrets is a really nasty pastime.

examples.ko: 친구를 놀라게 하는 게 그 사람의 악취미예요.
examples.en: Scaring his friends is his nasty hobby.
I think that kind of prank is in bad taste.

examples.ko: 제 옷 취향이 악취미라고 놀리는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who teases me that my taste in clothes is awful.

examples.ko: 악취미를 가진 사람처럼 일부러 남을 곤란하게 해요.
examples.en: He deliberately puts others in a bind, like someone with a nasty hobby.

examples.ko: 남이 실수하는 걸 보며 웃는 건 악취미 같아요.
examples.en: Laughing at others' mistakes seems like a nasty habit.

explain: 남을 불편하게 하거나 곤란하게 만드는 못된 취미나 버릇을 말해요. '취미'가 취향이라는 뜻으로도 쓰여서, 놀리듯이 취향이 나쁘다는 말로 쓰기도 해요. '~는 악취미예요'처럼 비판하는 말투로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Teasing people on purpose is a nasty habit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 끝내서 그 행동이 못됐다고 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite ending used to criticize a behavior as nasty.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 남의 일기를 읽는 악취미가 있어요.
phrases.en: That friend has a nasty habit of reading other people's diaries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 못된 버릇을 가졌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone has such a bad habit.

phrases.en: Please give up that nasty habit now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 못된 버릇을 그만두라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to stop a nasty habit.
phrases.en_equiv: to give up a nasty habit

explain_en: It means a mean hobby or habit that makes other people uncomfortable or puts them in a bind. Because '취미' can also mean taste, it is sometimes used teasingly to say someone's taste is bad. It is often used as a criticism, like '~는 악취미예요'.

t90.ax: Scaring his friends is his nasty hobby.

en: to be cautious; to be circumspect; to be careful

examples.en: That person handles work very carefully.
I prepared thoroughly, so there were no mistakes.
I made a careful plan before the trip.
My older sister is rather meticulous by nature.
Thanks to my well-prepared friend, we had an umbrella.

examples.ko: 너무 용의주도해서 좀 답답할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: He is so thorough that it can feel stifling sometimes.

explain: 빈틈없이 미리 준비하고 조심하는 사람이나 계획에 써요. 보통은 칭찬이지만 계산적인 느낌을 줄 때도 있어요. '용의주도하게 + 동사', '용의주도한 사람'으로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: He is a very careful and thorough person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form for describing a noun.

phrases.en: I wasn't careful enough, so I made a mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 준비가 부족했다고 반성할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to admit you were not prepared carefully enough.

phrases.en: His plans are meticulous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치밀하다'는 빈틈없이 꼼꼼하다는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word meaning meticulous and without gaps.

explain_en: It describes a person or plan that is carefully prepared in advance with no gaps. It is usually praise, but it can sometimes sound calculating. It is commonly used as '용의주도하게 + verb' or '용의주도한 사람'.

t90.ax: I made a careful plan before the trip.

en: to be hollow; to be sunken; to be concave

examples.ko: 땅이 우묵해서 비가 오면 물이 고여요.
examples.en: The ground is hollowed, so water collects when it rains.
Please put the soup in a deep, hollow bowl.
Your eyes look sunken, so you seem tired.
The spot where the ball fell has become dented.
The middle of the road is dipped, so be careful.

examples.ko: 우묵하다고 해서 다 깊은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because it is hollowed doesn't mean it is deep.

explain: 가운데가 안쪽으로 둥글게 들어간 모양에 써요. 일상 말로는 '움푹하다'나 '움푹 패다'를 더 자주 들을 수 있어요. 눈이 들어가 피곤해 보일 때는 '눈이 퀭하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Rainwater collected in the hollow spot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우묵하다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form used before a noun.

phrases.en: The middle of this plate looks sunken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이는 모양을 말할 때 '-아/어 보이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 보이다' describes how something looks.

phrases.en: This bowl is not very deep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양이 안쪽으로 들어가지 않았다고 말하는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This negative form says something is not hollowed in.

explain_en: It describes a shape whose middle sinks inward in a rounded way. In everyday speech you may hear '움푹하다' or '움푹 패다' more often. For sunken, tired-looking eyes people also say '눈이 퀭하다'.

t90.ax: Your eyes look sunken, so you seem tired.

en: to be very risky; to be very perilous

examples.ko: 아이가 난간 위에 서 있어서 위태위태해요.
examples.en: The child is standing on the railing, so it looks very precarious.
There is a rumor that the company's situation is shaky.
Watching him walk so unsteadily made me nervous.

examples.ko: 짐을 너무 높이 쌓아서 위태위태해 보여요.
examples.en: The load is piled so high that it looks like it could fall.
His health is in a precarious state.
The score gap was small, so it was nerve-racking.

explain: '위태하다'를 반복해서 곧 무너지거나 떨어질 것처럼 아슬아슬한 느낌을 더 생생하게 말해요. '아슬아슬하다'와 비슷하지만, 건강·회사·관계처럼 눈에 안 보이는 상황에도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 아이가 자전거를 타는 모습이 위태위태해 보여요.
phrases.en: The child riding a bicycle looks very precarious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습을 보고 불안하게 느낄 때 '-아/어 보이다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-아/어 보이다' when something looks precarious from the outside.

phrases.example: 그는 절벽 끝에 위태위태하게 서 있어요.
phrases.en: He is standing precariously at the edge of the cliff.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 서 있거나 걷는 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-게' describes how someone stands or moves.

phrases.en: The relationship between the two is in danger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반복하지 않은 기본형이고, '위태위태하다'보다 느낌이 덜 생생해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The base form without repetition, less vivid than '위태위태하다'.

explain_en: It repeats '위태하다' to give a vivid sense of something about to collapse or fall. It is close to '아슬아슬하다', but it is also often used for things you cannot see, such as health, a company or a relationship.

en: to be narrow in the middle; to be nipped in

examples.ko: 허리가 잘록해서 이 원피스가 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Her waist is narrow, so this dress suits her well.
This bottle is shaped so that it narrows in the middle.
An hourglass has a shape that is pinched in the middle.
That island is narrow in the middle.

examples.ko: 잘록한 허리선을 강조하는 옷이 요즘 유행이에요.
examples.en: Clothes that emphasize a slim waistline are in fashion these days.

examples.ko: 산 가운데가 잘록했던 곳에 작은 마을이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a small village where the mountain narrowed in the middle.

explain: 허리나 병의 목처럼 가운데가 쏙 들어간 모양에 써요. 허리가 잘록하다는 말은 날씬하다는 칭찬으로도 자주 들려요. 반대로 가운데가 볼록하게 나오면 '불룩하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: It's an outfit that shows off a slim waist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양이에요. 허리가 날씬하게 들어간 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun; describes a slimly narrowed waist.

phrases.en: This vase is narrow in the middle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 서술형이에요. 물건의 가운데가 쏙 들어간 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite predicate form; describes an object that narrows in the middle.

phrases.example: 이 병은 가운데가 잘록하지 않고 곧게 내려와요.
phrases.en: This bottle isn't narrow in the middle; it goes straight down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가운데가 들어가지 않았다고 부정할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say the middle does not narrow in.
phrases.en_equiv: is not narrow in the middle

explain_en: It describes a shape that is pinched in the middle, like a waist or the neck of a bottle. Saying someone's waist is 잘록하다 is often heard as a compliment about a slim figure. The opposite, bulging out in the middle, is '불룩하다'.

examples.en: We made an ad to increase potential customers.

examples.ko: 이 선수는 잠재 능력이 아주 커요.
examples.en: This player has great potential ability.
Please believe in the child's potential.

examples.ko: 회사는 시장의 잠재 가치를 높게 봤어요.
examples.en: The company rated the market's latent value highly.

examples.ko: 잠재 위험을 미리 알면 사고를 막을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you know hidden risks beforehand, you can prevent accidents.
That child has a lot of latent talent.

explain: '잠재'는 아직 겉으로 드러나지 않고 속에 숨어 있다는 뜻으로 '잠재력', '잠재 고객'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 써요. 혼자 쓰는 일은 드물어요. 이미 겉으로 드러난 것은 '실제'라고 해서 비교하면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: This child has great potential.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잠재'가 들어간 가장 흔한 말로, 속에 있는 힘이나 가능성을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word with 잠재, meaning hidden power or possibility.

phrases.en: We showed the ad to potential customers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 물건을 사지 않았지만 앞으로 살 수 있는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: People who haven't bought yet but might in the future.

phrases.en: They say dreams are related to the subconscious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 알지 못하지만 마음속에 있는 생각을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Thoughts inside the mind that a person is not aware of.

explain_en: Base noun for hidden, not yet visible ability or state, often before another noun (잠재 능력). 잠재 means hidden inside and not yet visible, and it is used in front of another word as in 잠재력 or 잠재 고객. It is rarely used alone. Something that already shows is called 실제 (actual), which helps as a contrast.

t90.ax: That child has a lot of latent talent.

examples.ko: 그 농구 선수는 장신인데도 움직임이 빨라요.
examples.en: That basketball player is tall yet moves quickly.

examples.ko: 장신 선수들이 많은 팀이 리바운드에 유리해요.
examples.en: A team with many tall players has an advantage in rebounding.

examples.ko: 동생은 어릴 때부터 장신이라서 눈에 띄었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling stood out from a young age because of being tall.
The tallest person in our class is Minsu.
Tall models walked onto the stage.

examples.ko: 장신 군단을 상대로 힘든 경기를 했어요.
examples.en: We played a tough game against a team of tall players.

explain: '키가 크다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '장신'은 농구·배구 선수나 모델처럼 키가 큰 사람을 소개할 때 주로 써요. 반대말은 '단신'이에요. 자기 자신을 말할 때는 '키가 커요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 우리 배구팀에는 장신 선수가 세 명 있어요.
phrases.en: Our volleyball team has three tall players.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장신'은 이렇게 '선수'와 함께 써서 키 큰 사람을 소개할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 장신 is often paired with 선수 to introduce someone who is tall.

phrases.example: 그 모델은 장신이라서 어떤 옷도 잘 어울려요.
phrases.en: That model is tall, so any clothes look good on her.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장신이다'의 연결형으로, 키가 큰 것이 이유일 때 써요. 다른 사람을 설명할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a connective form of 장신이다, used when being tall is the reason, mostly when describing another person.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is tall, so he is good at basketball.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장신'과 같은 뜻을 일상에서 쓰는 말로, 자기 자신을 말할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the everyday way to say the same thing as 장신, and it also works when talking about yourself.

explain_en: '키가 크다' is the everyday expression, while '장신' is mainly used to introduce tall people such as basketball or volleyball players and models. Its opposite is '단신'. When talking about yourself, '키가 커요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: That person is the right fit for the team leader position.
A meticulous person is just right for this job.

examples.ko: 적격 심사를 통과해야 계약할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to pass the eligibility review to sign the contract.

examples.ko: 심사 결과 두 팀이 적격으로 판정됐어요.
examples.en: After the review, two teams were judged eligible.
What kind of person would be right for this role?

examples.ko: 그는 선생님으로서 적격은 아닌 것 같아요.
examples.en: I don't think he is suited to be a teacher.

explain: 주로 '~에 적격이다'로 쓰고, 자격이나 조건에 딱 맞는다는 판단이 담겨 있어요. 반의어는 '부적격'이에요.

phrases.en: That person is the right fit for this job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 문형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern.

phrases.en: We are looking for a qualified person for this post.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자격에 맞는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a qualified person.

phrases.en: That candidate was judged unqualified.
phrases.nuance_ko: '적격'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 적격.

explain_en: Fully qualified or ideal for a role or post. It is mostly used as '~에 적격이다' and carries a judgment that someone or something fits the qualifications or conditions exactly. Its opposite is '부적격'.

examples.en: An unidentified sound is heard every night.
An unidentified letter was in the mailbox.
Everyone was wary because the man's identity was unknown.

examples.ko: 정체불명의 전화는 받지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to answer calls from unknown numbers.
An unidentified object appeared in the news.

examples.ko: 정체불명 가게에서 이상한 물건을 팔고 있었어요.
examples.en: A mysterious shop was selling strange things.

explain: 주로 '정체불명의 + 명사' 형태로 써요. 누구인지 무엇인지 모르고 조금 수상한 느낌이 있어요. 그냥 모를 때는 '모르는'이라고 하고, '정체불명'은 뉴스나 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 정체불명의 사람이 집 앞에 서 있었어요.
phrases.en: An unidentified person was standing in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구인지 모르고 조금 수상한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person whose identity is unknown and a bit suspicious.

phrases.en: An unidentified package came to the office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보낸 사람을 모르는 물건에도 '정체불명의'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for objects when you don't know where they came from.

phrases.example: 정체를 알 수 없는 냄새가 나요.
phrases.en: There's a smell I can't identify.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정체불명보다 풀어서 쓴 말이라 대화에서 더 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A looser way to say it, more comfortable in conversation.

explain_en: It mostly appears as 정체불명의 + noun. It carries a slightly suspicious feel, not just not knowing. For ordinary unknowns people say 모르는, while 정체불명 shows up more in news and stories.

en: to be demure; to behave modestly and properly

examples.ko: 그 학생은 말과 행동이 조신해서 칭찬을 받아요.
examples.en: That student is well-mannered in word and deed, so he gets praised.
Grandmother sat quietly and properly while drinking her tea.

examples.ko: 조신한 태도 덕분에 면접관에게 좋은 인상을 줬어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my composed manner, I made a good impression on the interviewer.
I was taught to behave properly in front of elders.
My mother scolded me for not behaving properly.
I was surprised that the child suddenly became so well-behaved.

explain: '얌전하다'와 비슷하지만 말과 행동을 삼가고 예의 바르게 처신한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 예전에는 여성에게 많이 썼던 말이라, 요즘 칭찬으로 쓰면 성별 고정관념처럼 들릴 수도 있어서 조심해요.

phrases.en: I tried to behave modestly and properly at the interview.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조신하다'를 '-게'로 이어서 행동을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This uses the '-게' form to describe how someone acts.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 조신한 태도로 어른들께 인사했어요.
phrases.en: She greeted the elders with a modest and proper manner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조신한'은 뒤에 명사가 와서 사람의 태도나 모습을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '조신한' form comes before a noun to describe someone's manner.

phrases.en: My child is well-behaved when guests come.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조신하다'와 비슷하지만 더 쉽고 자주 쓰는 말이에요. 예의보다 조용하고 차분한 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar but easier and more common word. It stresses being quiet and calm more than being polite.
phrases.en_equiv: to be well-behaved; to be quiet and gentle

explain_en: It is similar to '얌전하다' (quiet and well-behaved) but has a stronger sense of being careful and polite in speech and conduct. It was often used about women in the past, so praising someone with it today can sound like a gender stereotype; be careful.

examples.en: Our team was unbeatable this year.

examples.ko: 아이는 히어로 옷을 입고 천하무적이 된 것처럼 뛰어다녀요.
examples.en: The child runs around in a hero costume as if he were invincible.

examples.ko: 아무리 천하무적인 팀이라도 방심하면 질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even an unbeatable team can lose if it lets its guard down.
In the game, this character is called invincible.

examples.ko: 천하무적이던 선수도 부상 앞에서는 어쩔 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Even the once-invincible player was helpless against injury.

examples.ko: 엄마 앞에서는 천하무적 아빠도 꼼짝 못 해요.
examples.en: Even invincible Dad can't make a move in front of Mom.

explain: '최강'과 비슷하지만 '천하무적'은 맞설 상대가 없다는 과장되고 장난스러운 느낌이 있어요. '천하무적이다'처럼 서술어로도, '천하무적 군대'처럼 명사 앞에서도 써요. 아이들 놀이나 응원에서 가볍게 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: In this game, I am invincible.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 써서 상대가 없을 만큼 강하다고 장난스럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a predicate to playfully say one is so strong that nobody can match them.

phrases.en: The child likes stories about an invincible hero.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 아주 강한 인물이나 팀을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe a very strong character or team.

phrases.en: The child shouted loudly as if invincible.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처럼'을 붙이면 실제가 아니라 그런 기분이라는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 처럼 means it is a feeling, not reality.

explain_en: Unrivaled — so strong nobody can match, a four-character idiom (우리 팀은 너무 강해서 천하무적이라는 말까지 나왔어요.) It is similar to '최강' (the strongest), but '천하무적' has an exaggerated, playful feel of having no rival at all. It can be a predicate, as in '천하무적이다', or sit before a noun, as in '천하무적 군대'. People also use it lightly in kids' games and cheering.

t90.ax: Our team was unbeatable this year.

en: to be very odd; to be extremely strange; to be bizarre

examples.en: I had a bizarre dream this morning.
That person's behavior is so bizarre.

examples.ko: 어른들이 보시기에 그 옷차림은 해괴했나 봐요.
examples.en: That outfit must have looked outlandish to the elders.
A strange-looking fish was caught in the net.
Everyone says that rule is absurdly strange.
It was so bizarre that I couldn't even laugh.

explain: '이상하다'보다 훨씬 센 말이에요. 어이없고 못마땅한 느낌이 들어서 소문, 일, 옷차림 같은 것에 써요. 사람에게 직접 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '이상하다', '황당하다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: A bizarre rumor went around the neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿기 어려울 만큼 이상한 이야기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for stories so strange they are hard to believe.

phrases.en: He showed up in a bizarre outfit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모습이 어이없을 만큼 이상할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's appearance is absurdly strange.

phrases.en: I'm really baffled to hear about such a thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해괴하다'보다 일상에서 더 부담 없이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier to use in daily life than 해괴하다.

explain_en: So strange it is shocking or disturbing; more literary/formal (해괴한 소문) It is much stronger than '이상하다' (strange), with a feeling of disbelief and disapproval, used for rumors, events or outfits. Said directly about a person it can sound rude. In daily speech people use '이상하다' or '황당하다' more often.

t90.ax: I had a bizarre dream this morning.

examples.en: My appearance was shabby, so I hesitated to go in.

examples.ko: 그는 행색은 허름해도 마음은 따뜻한 사람이에요.
examples.en: He may look shabby, but he has a warm heart.

examples.ko: 사람을 행색만 보고 판단하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't judge people just by how they look.

examples.ko: 비에 젖은 행색을 보고 직원이 수건을 가져다줬어요.
examples.en: Seeing how soaked I looked, the staff member brought me a towel.

examples.ko: 이런 행색으로 결혼식에 갈 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't go to a wedding looking like this.
I could sense traces of hardship in his appearance.

explain: '옷차림'은 입은 옷을 말하지만 '행색'은 옷과 몰골을 합친 전체 모습이에요. 주로 '초라하다', '허름하다'처럼 좋지 않은 모습을 말할 때 많이 써요. '차림새'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 때도 있지만 '행색'이 더 안 좋은 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 그는 초라한 행색으로 가게 문 앞에 서 있었어요.
phrases.en: He stood at the shop door looking shabby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태로, 가난하고 볼품없는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form describing a poor, unimpressive look.

phrases.example: 행색이 남루한 노인이 길가에 앉아 있었어요.
phrases.en: An old man in ragged clothes was sitting by the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이 낡고 해진 모습을 좀 더 글 같은 말투로 표현해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A somewhat literary way to describe worn, tattered clothes and look.

phrases.example: 사람을 행색만 보고 판단하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't judge people only by how they look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습으로 사람을 평가하는 것을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about judging people by their outward look.

explain_en: Literary — how someone looks via clothing and state (초라한 행색) '옷차림' is about the clothes you wear, but '행색' is the overall look of clothes and condition together. It is mostly used for a poor or shabby look, with words like '초라하다' and '허름하다'. '차림새' can sometimes replace it, but '행색' leans more negative.

t90.ax: I can't go to a wedding looking like this.

en: to be similar; to be alike; to resemble

examples.en: The two people's voices are really alike.
This painting looked just like the real one.
The son walks with a gait very like his father's.

examples.ko: 그 사건은 작년에 일어난 일과 흡사할 거예요.
examples.en: That incident is probably much like what happened last year.
The dream was so close to reality that it was scary.

examples.ko: 쌍둥이처럼 흡사하게 생긴 두 가게가 나란히 있어요.
examples.en: Two shops that look as alike as twins stand side by side.

explain: '비슷하다'보다 딱딱하고 '거의 같다'에 가까워요. 보통 '~와 흡사하다'로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '닮았다', '비슷하다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The two buildings are very similar in shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흡사하다'가 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 활용형으로, 거의 같은 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, describing a nearly identical appearance.

phrases.example: 두 사람의 성격은 별로 흡사하지 않아요.
phrases.en: The two people's personalities are not very alike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지 않다고 말할 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say two things are not alike.

phrases.en: My face looks a lot like my dad's.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흡사하다'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used far more often than 흡사하다 in everyday conversation.

explain_en: Literary; strong resemblance, like voices or faces. This is a stiffer, more written word than '비슷하다' and leans toward 'almost identical'. It is usually used as '~와 흡사하다'; in everyday speech people more often say '닮았다' or '비슷하다'.

t90.ax: The two people's voices are really alike.
